--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Validate.col_vals_chat_format()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: >- Validate whether column values are well-formed chat conversations. twitter-card: title: >- [Validate.col_vals_chat_format()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: >- Validate whether column values are well-formed chat conversations. title: >- [Validate.col_vals_chat_format()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Validate whether column values are well-formed chat conversations. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Validate whether column values are well-formed chat conversations. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/validate.py#L15587-L15838){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Validate.col_vals_chat_format( columns, roles=("system", "user", "assistant"), alternate=True, first_role=None, last_role=None, allow_empty=False, role_key="role", content_key="content", na_pass=False, pre=None, segments=None, thresholds=None, actions=None, brief=None, active=True, dimension=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The `col_vals_chat_format()` validation method checks that each value of a column is a well-formed conversation of the kind used to fine-tune a chat model: a list of messages, each with a role and some content. Each row is a test unit, and a row fails if its value isn't a list of messages, has a message without a role or with a role that isn't in `roles=`, has a system message anywhere but first, has turns that don't alternate between roles, starts or ends with the wrong role, or has a message without content. Malformed conversations are common in chat data that's been converted from other formats, and a training run can fail on them, or silently learn from them. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | Column | ColumnSelector | ColumnSelectorNarwhals]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A single column or a list of columns to validate. Can also use [`col()`](`pointblank.col`) with column selectors to specify one or more columns. If multiple columns are supplied or resolved, there will be a separate validation step generated for each column. The values are lists of messages (such as a Polars column of lists of structs, or a pandas column of lists of dictionaries) or the JSON text of them, either as a list or as an object with a `"messages"` key. [roles]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Sequence[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(["system"]{.st}, ["user"]{.st}, ["assistant"]{.st})]{.doc-parameter-default} : The roles that a message can have. The default is `("system", "user", "assistant")`. If `"system"` is one of them, a system message can only be the first message. [alternate]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Should the turns (the messages after a first system message) alternate, so that no role follows itself? The default is `True`. [first_role]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The role of the first turn (the first message after a system message), such as `"user"`. The default, `None`, doesn't check it. [last_role]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The role of the last message, such as `"assistant"` (for a conversation that ends with the reply that a model should learn). The default, `None`, doesn't check it. [allow_empty]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Can a message have empty content (missing, or only whitespace)? The default is `False`. [role_key]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["role"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The key of the role in each message. The default is `"role"`. [content_key]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["content"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The key of the content in each message. The default is `"content"`. [na_pass]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Should a missing value pass? The default is `False`. [pre]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Callable | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional preprocessing function or lambda to apply to the data table during interrogation. This function should take a table as input and return a modified table. [segments]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [SegmentSpec | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional directive on segmentation, which serves to split a validation step into multiple (one step per segment). Can be a single column name, a tuple that specifies a column name and its corresponding values to segment on, or a combination of both (provided as a list). [thresholds]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | float | bool | tuple | dict | Thresholds | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Set threshold failure levels for reporting and reacting to exceedences of the levels. The thresholds are set at the step level and will override any global thresholds set in `Validate(thresholds=...)`. The default is `None`, which means that no thresholds will be set locally and global thresholds (if any) will take effect. [actions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Actions | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional actions to take when the validation step meets or exceeds any set threshold levels. If provided, the [`Actions`](`pointblank.Actions`) class should be used to define the actions. [brief]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional brief description of the validation step that will be displayed in the reporting table. You can use the templating elements like `"{step}"` to insert the step number, or `"{auto}"` to include an automatically generated brief. If `True` the entire brief will be automatically generated. If `None` (the default) then there won't be a brief. [active]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | Callable]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A boolean value or callable that determines whether the validation step should be active. Using `False` will make the validation step inactive (still reporting its presence and keeping indexes for the steps unchanged). A callable can also be provided; it will receive the data table as its single argument and must return a boolean value. The callable is evaluated *before* any `pre=` processing. [dimension]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional data quality dimension to categorize this validation step for health scoring. One of `"completeness"`, `"validity"`, `"uniqueness"`, `"consistency"`, `"timeliness"`, or `"volume"` (or any custom string). If `None` (the default), the dimension is `"validity"`. This label appears in the validation report and feeds the overall and per-dimension health scores. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Validate]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The `Validate` object with the added validation step. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `roles=` isn't a list of role names, or if `role_key=` or `content_key=` isn't a string. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `roles=` is empty, or if `first_role=` or `last_role=` isn't one of `roles=`. ::: ## The Problems Found {.doc-the-problems-found} The first problem found with a conversation is in a column of the results called `pb_reason_`, which is in the extracts of failing rows and in the step report. The step's note says how many rows have each problem. The problems are checked in this order: - `not_messages`: the value isn't a list of messages (or the JSON text of one) - `no_messages`: the list of messages is empty - `bad_message`: a message isn't a mapping with a role (under `role_key=`) that's a string - `unknown_role`: a message has a role that isn't in `roles=` - `system_position`: a system message isn't the first message - `first_role`: the first turn doesn't have the role of `first_role=` - `not_alternating`: a role follows itself (with `alternate=True`) - `last_role`: the last message doesn't have the role of `last_role=` - `empty_content`: a message has no content, or content that's only whitespace (unless `allow_empty=True`) A Polars or pandas column can hold the messages as lists (of structs or dictionaries) or as JSON text. For a database table (through Ibis) or a PySpark DataFrame, the column must hold JSON text: its distinct values are collected and checked, and the problems are joined back to the table on its own backend. ## Examples {.doc-examples} For the examples here, we'll use a small table of conversations, stored as JSON text. ::: {#fed353f0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl tbl = pl.DataFrame( { "id": [1, 2, 3, 4], "messages": [ '[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi!"}, ' '{"role": "assistant", "content": "Hello! How can I help?"}]', '[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi!"}, {"role": "user", "content": "Hello?"}]', '[{"role": "system", "content": "Be brief."}, ' '{"role": "user", "content": "Capital of France?"}, ' '{"role": "assistant", "content": "Paris."}]', '[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2 + 2?"}, ' '{"role": "bot", "content": "4"}]', ], } ) ``` ::: Let's validate that each conversation is well formed and ends with a reply of the assistant. ::: {#10e067c3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} validation = ( pb.Validate(data=tbl) .col_vals_chat_format(columns="messages", last_role="assistant") .interrogate() ) validation ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
